input: Book connecting train tickets for the coastal trip

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the full route — origin, destination, and any intermediate stops — determines how many legs need to be booked and whether a single operator covers them all.
The travel date and time of day affects which trains are available, connection viability, and whether peak/off-peak pricing applies.
The number and type of passengers (adults, children, seniors, railcard holders) directly changes pricing, seat requirements, and booking complexity.
A budget ceiling or a fixed maximum connection time limit narrows which ticket options and fare classes are viable.
Preferences such as seat class, window vs. aisle, direct vs. fastest vs. cheapest route, and flexibility to change tickets shape which booking options to prioritise.
Knowing whether to book through a specific platform, app, or rail operator (and whether e-tickets are acceptable) determines the exact booking method to use.
Understanding what a successful booking looks like — guaranteed connections, specific arrival window, all tickets under one booking reference — defines what done well means.

gold.taskTitle: Book connecting train tickets for coastal trip
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to book a multi-leg train journey with connecting services for a coastal trip.

questions.title: What is the full route, including origin and destination stations?
questions.description: Identify the departure station, arrival station, and any required intermediate stops to map out all the legs that need to be booked.

questions.title: What date and approximate time do you need to travel?
questions.description: Pin down the travel date and preferred departure or arrival time so that available train services and connection windows can be identified.

questions.title: How many passengers are travelling, and do any hold railcards?
questions.description: Confirm the number and type of travellers — adults, children, seniors — and any discount cards, as these affect pricing and seat allocation.

questions.title: Is there a maximum budget you want to stay within?
questions.description: Establish a price ceiling per person or in total to filter fare classes and booking options accordingly.

questions.title: Do you prefer the cheapest fare, the fastest journey, or flexible tickets?
questions.description: Understand whether cost, travel time, or the ability to change/cancel tickets is the top priority when selecting between available options.

questions.title: Which platform or app should the booking be made through?
questions.description: Determine whether to use a specific rail operator's site, a third-party aggregator, or a mobile app, and whether e-tickets or physical tickets are needed.

questions.title: Do you need all legs under one booking reference to protect connections?
questions.description: Clarify whether the connecting tickets must be linked under a single booking so that delays on one leg are covered by the operator for the next.
